clue.text: Bradman, Australian cricket star, starts up — one not out

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
the starts of the four words name their first letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: A tribute to Don Bradman's batting, starting off with a cricket star who was never dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' gives BACS from the four words, and 'up' turns that round. 'One not out' looks like a cricket batsman unbeaten, but it is a worker who refuses to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker is a worker who carries on rather than coming out on strike with colleagues.

clue.text: A party shortly to enter meeting with set of statistics

indicators.note: to enter means these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
taken as written

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: A brief get-together is fitted into a meeting along with a pile of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the last letter of the party word, and 'to enter' splits the meeting word around the A and the trimmed party.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is a structured collection of data, such as statistics, held for retrieval.

clue.text: It's said to go the other way, which is up

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: to turn is to go the other way, change direction

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that reverses direction and yet stays aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout this puzzle 'which is up' or 'something up' means a bird, up in the air; here it looks like part of the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird flies overhead, so in this puzzle's convention a bird is something that is up in the sky.

clue.text: Emu wasn't all of a flutter, though something up

indicators.note: all of a flutter means agitated and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An emu was not flustered, though another creature was in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all of a flutter' shuffles EMUWASNT. 'something up' means a flying bird, the puzzle's running theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A mute swan is a large white bird, and a flying bird is something up in the sky.

clue.text: Worshipper of western India has standard to observe

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
to see is to observe

explanation.surface: A devotee from western India keeps a norm and watches.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsees are followers of Zoroastrianism living mainly in Mumbai and western India.

clue.text: Royal woman in tree, which is up

parts.note: a king is a royal

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the tree

parts.note: a fir is a tree
she is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A royal lady is perched up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the woman inside the tree. Throughout this puzzle 'which is up' means a bird, up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured river bird, so a creature that flies up in the air.

clue.text: One with an affected attitude regrets work, which is up

indicators.note: in a down clue, being up means the letters run bottom to top, so they are read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone striking an attitude laments a piece of work that's flown high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' turns RUESOP right round. Elsewhere in the puzzle 'which is up' signals a bird, but here it is a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur behaves affectedly to impress, putting on airs that are not genuine.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, is left without newspaper

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without means the newspaper's letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A man is abandoned with nothing to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the newspaper's letters. Man is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an island, so Man stands for the general term.

clue.text: One lifting something up

definitions.meaning: a hoisting machine that raises heavy loads on a building site
a tall wading bird, up in the air as birds are in this puzzle

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a lifting machine and a long-legged bird, each fitting one definition.

clue.text: As one man is on, two posh characters off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: U is the letter for upper-class, posh, usage, so two of them give UU

explanation.surface: A single man gets on while two snobs get off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' mixes MANISON with UU. 'As one' sounds like counting people but means in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as one means acting with complete agreement, every person of the same view.

clue.text: Thick, black and dry?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
rainless weather is dry

explanation.surface: A description of something dense, dark and parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' looks like a physical texture beside 'black and dry', but it means stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick is informal for stupid, and someone brainless lacks intelligence.

clue.text: English composer backing something up

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: An English composer supports an airborne cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns EBERG round. 'something up' is the puzzle's flying bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A grebe is a diving water bird, which in this puzzle counts as something up in the sky.

clue.text: Get down what may be up

definitions.meaning: to get food down the throat, to gulp it
a fork-tailed bird that may be up in the air

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to gulp down food and a fork-tailed migrating bird.

clue.text: Direction taken in search, which is up

indicators.note: taken in means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to sift is to search through carefully
W, west, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A compass bearing is included in a hunt for something overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: W is 'taken in' SIFT. 'which is up' means a bird in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift is a fast bird that spends almost all its life in flight, up in the sky.

clue.text: Layering process hit single state

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a nation is a state

explanation.surface: A process of building up layers strikes one country.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamination is the making of something by bonding thin layers together.

clue.text: Quip spread from the west about even parts of Spain

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other
in an across clue, from the west means reading right to left, so backwards

parts.note: marge, short for margarine, is a spread

indicators.note: even parts of means the second and fourth letters are taken

explanation.surface: A joke spreads from the west of Spain to its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the west' turns MARGE into EGRAM; 'even parts of' Spain gives PI, and EGRAM goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying, a pointed quip.

clue.text: Many confused over height, which is up

indicators.note: over means placed above, in a down clue, so the first piece comes first
confused means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Many in a muddle over a height, as if bewildered by something lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the first word's letters, and 'over' sets them above the height letter. 'which is up' means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A mynah is a starling from Asia famous for mimicking speech, a bird so up in the air.

clue.text: Setter's happiness evident with joist

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, and the 's stands for is
to beam is to show happiness visibly

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is smiling, pleased with a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Setter is happiness evident': I beam. The setter is the puzzle's compiler, who is I.
explanation.definitionFit: An I-beam is a steel girder with an I-shaped section, used as a joist.

clue.text: Country loses way with negative word

indicators.note: loses means these letters are taken out

parts.note: Norway is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation loses its path along with a word of refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor is a conjunction used after neither or with negatives, a negative connecting word.

clue.text: One furious with press, given reaction

indicators.note: furious, wild and violent, means the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A man angry with the press gives his reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' sits between the two fodder words and mixes ONEPRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reaction to something said or done.

clue.text: Great man heads north, which is up

indicators.note: heads means goes in front of, so the first piece leads

parts.note: a hero is a great man

explanation.surface: A great man travels north, high in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' looks like a verb of travel but places HERO before N. 'which is up' is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird, one of the puzzle's flying creatures.

clue.text: Get back on journey unfinished the night before

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a trip is a journey
eve is the evening or day before an event

explanation.surface: A traveller fetches something left on an incomplete trip the night before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts TRIP to TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve something is to get it back or recover it.

clue.text: She went down — a not entirely pleasant ending to what is up

indicators.note: ending to means this piece comes after the bird, at its end

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, and birds are what is up in this puzzle
taken as written

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A ship sank, a rather unhappy end to its voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims NICE to NIC; A plus NIC are the 'ending to' TIT. 'She went down' refers to the liner that sank in 1912, ships being called she.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the famous liner that sank in 1912, and ships are referred to as she.

clue.text: Make out vessel, which is up

indicators.note: make, as in make over, means the letters are refashioned into a new order

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel

explanation.surface: Discern a boat that's overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' looks like a single verb meaning discern, but 'Make' rearranges OUT as TOU. 'which is up' is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A toucan is a tropical bird with a huge colourful bill, so it flies up in the trees.

clue.text: Round the bend, something up

definitions.meaning: a British idiom for mad, crazy
a bird known for laying eggs in other nests, up in the air

explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for crazy and also names a bird known for its two-note call.

clue.text: Take up more space, with time inside

definitions.meaning: to extend or spread out further

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to extend in size and, informally, a term of imprisonment.

clue.text: Reckon to make a difference

definitions.meaning: to reckon is to calculate or tot up numbers

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to calculate a total and to matter or be significant.

clue.text: Chew the fat, which is up

definitions.meaning: an idiom for talking idly together
a small songbird such as the stonechat, up in the air

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an idle conversation and is also the name of several small songbirds.

clue.text: Pass notice, which is up

parts.note: to cross is to pass over
a bill is a posted notice

explanation.surface: Walk past a poster that's been put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is up' looks like it describes the notice stuck on a wall, but it means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbill is a finch whose bill tips cross over, a bird that is up in the air.

clue.text: Face in the distance, which is up

indicators.note: in a down clue, being up means reading bottom to top, so backwards
in means the letters lie hidden inside these words

explanation.surface: A face seen far off, high above.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EDIS run 'in' tHE DIStance; 'which is up' reverses them. Here the puzzle's bird phrase is a reversal instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a face of a solid shape, such as one face of a cube.

clue.text: Bit of fun, which is up

definitions.meaning: a prank or caper done for amusement
a songbird famous for singing high in the air

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a frolic or prank and also the songbird that sings while ascending.

clue.text: Similar mark in an Antipodean country

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the mark inside the country

parts.note: Aus is short for Australia, in the Antipodes
a logo is a trademark or emblem

explanation.surface: A similar brand is found in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the mark inside the country. The Antipodes is a British name for Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous means comparable or alike in some respect.

clue.text: One going down, which is up

definitions.meaning: a water bird, the loon, which also flies up in the air

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both someone who dives underwater and a type of diving water bird.
